correctness.rationale: Exact facial classification and the contractible-simplex homotopy pushouts reduce the core to \(S^{k+l-1}\) vee \(S^k\) vee \(S^l\); null-homotopic cone attachments on the disconnected pair of cross-polytope spheres add \(S^k\), \(S^l\) and one \(S^1\) each, and remaining singleton edges add \(\binom{s}{2}\) circles. The connectedness hypothesis for both attaching spheres holds because \(k,l\ge2\). The resulting integral homotopy splitting follows without torsion assumptions. Standalone exhaustive GF(2) face/boundary test of 14 cases, 4855 faces, independently confirms predicted reduced Betti vectors; computation alone is not the proof.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial interaction between TWO internal matching parts yields a unique top sphere in degree \(k+l-1\), in addition to s+1 spheres in each of degrees \(k,l\) and a free circle rank binom(s+1,2). Neither the single matched-part join formula nor broad shellability results predicts this new sphere. This gives a complete integral homotopy classification with independent unbounded parameters and a geometrically motivated top-dimensional interaction.
